the biological rhythm of the peripheral blood lymphocyte count is opposite to the biological rhythm of plasma cortisol.

the spontaneous lymphocyte proliferation and the lymphocyte proliferative response to phytohemagglutinin and concanavalin were found to vary during a 24-hour day in healthy male volunteers, and the peak values were found to be at 8.00 am and 8.00 pm and the lowest values at 2.00 pm.

the biological rhythm of the peripheral blood lymphocyte response to PHA and PPD was inversely related to the rhythm of plasma cortisol, and the response of lymphocytes to Con A varied directly with plasma cortisol.

the biological rhythm of cell mediated immunity in man.

the biological rhythm of the lymphocyte transformation is biphasic, with peak values at 08.000 and 20.000 hr, and a significant depression at 14.000 hr, whereas the response to PPD was highest at 02.000 hr.
the biological rhythm of spontaneous lymphocyte transformation, lymphocyte response to PHA, Con A and PPD, plasma cortisol and lymphocyte count are in phase with the 24-hr cycle.
the spontaneous lymphocyte response and the response to PHA and PPD are influenced by the biological rhythm of plasma cortisol.

the biological rhythm in cell mediated immunity in man may be related to the circadian rhythm of plasma cortisol.
the biological rhythm of the lymphocyte response was dependent on the biological rhythm of plasma cortisol.
the lymphocyte transformation and lymphocyte response to PHA and PPD are influenced by the biological rhythm of the body.

the biological rhythms of the immune system are more complicated than previously thought.
there is a significant circadian variation in the immune parameters studied.
the biological rhythms of lymphocyte transformation and lymphocyte response to PPD, Con A and PHA are different and are related to the biological clock.
